claims: Artemis II is a 10-day first-crewed flight test of NASA’s Orion spacecraft and Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
Artemis II will carry four astronauts around the Moon and back.
Artemis II will verify all spacecraft systems—including life support—in deep space.
The primary purpose of Artemis II is testing the Orion spacecraft's life-support, navigation, and propulsion systems with a crew on board.
Artemis II will take four astronauts on a free-return trajectory around the Moon.
Artemis II will reach up to 252,760 miles from Earth.
Artemis II will come within roughly 4,000 miles of the lunar surface.
Astronauts will manually operate and test the Orion spacecraft on Artemis II.
Artemis II involves conducting in-flight human health studies.
Artemis II includes crew from both NASA and the Canadian Space Agency (CSA).
The crew of Artemis II is Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch (NASA), and Jeremy Hansen (CSA).
Artemis II will launch from Kennedy Space Center, FL, on the SLS rocket.
Artemis II trajectory includes translunar injection to circle the Moon and return for a Pacific Ocean splashdown.
Artemis II is the first crewed Artemis mission.
Artemis II is the first crewed mission beyond low Earth orbit since 1972.
